Dockerfile.text:
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY store.mjs page.mjs server.mjs ./
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown node /data
USER node
ENV PORT=8080 STATE=/tmp/state.json
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz || exit 1
CMD ["node", "server.mjs"]

README.md.text:
# sign-keeper

After using this, you can now **send a document link, get a typed-name signature with recorded consent, and keep a certificate anyone can re-verify**, on a server you own. That used to mean a per-user or per-envelope e-signature plan that keeps your agreements in its account.

**Live tool:** https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/sign-keeper/

Two parts, both free and MIT:

- **`index.html`**: the product page with an in-browser tamper-check demo (clearly labelled sample data). Nothing is uploaded.
- **`server.mjs`**: the service. One Node process, **zero dependencies**, state in one JSON file.

## Why someone would use this

| Today | Cost / catch | Sign Keeper |
|---|---|---|
| DocuSign, Dropbox Sign, PandaDoc and similar | Per-user or per-envelope plans; documents and audit trail live with them | Unlimited requests, one JSON file you own, no fee |
| "Reply YES to confirm" | No fingerprint of what was agreed, no consent to e-sign on record | Text hashed, consent wording stored, certificate to keep |
| Print, sign, scan | Slow, easy to lose, no integrity check | A link and ninety seconds |

Honest limits: **simple (typed-name) electronic signatures only.** No identity verification, no PDF upload or field placement, no templates, reminders or multi-signer routing, one admin key, no email sending of its own (set `NOTIFY_WEBHOOK` for a chat ping). For regulated or high-value documents, or where a statute requires a stricter signature or paper, use a qualified provider. This is software, not legal advice.

## What it does

1. **Create** in `/admin` (or `POST /v1/requests` with `{title, body, signerName?, signerEmail?, days?}`): you get a signing link `…/s/<token>`; the token is 128 random bits and is the only access control, so send it only to the signer. Requests expire (default 14 days, max 90).
2. **Sign** at the link: the signer reads the text, types their name (it must match `signerName` if you set one) and ticks the consent to sign electronically. They can instead decline with a reason. Honeypot field, a per-visitor daily cap (HMAC-hashed address, never the raw one).
3. **Certificate** at `…/c/<token>` (printable) and `…/c/<token>.json`: signer name, time, the document's SHA-256, the audit trail and the chain head, with the integrity check recomputed on each load.
4. **Tamper evidence.** Every audit event (`created`, `viewed`, `signed`, `declined`, `voided`) hashes the previous one. Editing the text, an event, or the signature after the fact, or deleting an event, makes the check fail. It is tamper-*evident*, not tamper-*proof*: whoever controls the server file can still delete it, so keep copies of certificates.
5. **Reports.** `GET /v1/summary`, `GET /v1/requests` (no document bodies), `GET /v1/requests.csv` (formulas neutralised). A signed request cannot be voided.

## Run it

```sh
cd ventures/sign-keeper
node --test        # 14 tests, no network
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) PUBLIC_URL=https://sign.example.com COMPANY_NAME=Acme node server.mjs
```

| Env | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ADMIN_KEY`, `PUBLIC_URL` | required |
| `COMPANY_NAME`, `BRAND_COLOR` | wording and `#rrggbb` accent |
| `TRUST_PROXY` | `true` behind a reverse proxy so the daily cap uses `X-Forwarded-For` |
| `IP_SECRET` | key for the visitor hash (random per start if unset; set it to keep the hash stable across restarts) |
| `NOTIFY_WEBHOOK` | optional https webhook pinged when a request is signed or declined |
| `STATE` | path of the JSON state file |

Put it behind HTTPS before real use.

## One-click deploy (your own account)

Fork this repository and open `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>`. `render.yaml` builds the `Dockerfile` here in **your** Render account with a 1 GB disk and a generated `ADMIN_KEY`. Docker anywhere works, see `docker-compose.yml`; `fly.toml` is a Fly.io path. Nothing runs on the author's side.

## Status and what is not verified

Everything in `node --test` passes (store rules including tamper detection, HTTP flow, escaping). It has **not** been tried in real browsers or at real traffic by the author, and no lawyer has reviewed it. You are the operator: decide whether a typed-name signature is valid for your document and jurisdiction.

Files: `store.mjs` (rules and hash chain), `page.mjs` (signing page, certificate, admin), `server.mjs` (HTTP shell), `index.html` (product page).

VENTURE.yaml.text:
name: sign-keeper
description: >-
  Self-hosted e-signature requests: paste a document, send a link, the signer
  types their name and ticks a consent box, and you keep a certificate with the
  text's SHA-256 and a hash-chained audit trail anyone can re-verify.
  Zero-dependency server with a one-click Render deploy.
stage: prototype
owner: duncan

# Screened 2026-10-16. Paid market is large and per-seat: DocuSign, Dropbox Sign
# (HelloSign), PandaDoc, SignNow, Adobe Sign and SignWell charge per user or per
# envelope, and free tiers cap documents at a handful a month. The gap: a freelancer,
# agency or small landlord who sends a few simple agreements (NDAs, SOWs, approvals)
# and wants unlimited signing, no signer account, and a record they can prove
# unaltered, without paying per envelope. duplicate_check.py top score 0.30
# (proposal-maker, which writes the proposal; this collects the signature).
#
# Liability boundary: a simple (typed-name) electronic signature only; no identity
# verification, no claim any document is enforceable, "not legal advice" stated on
# the page, the certificate and the README. The audit trail is tamper-evident, not
# tamper-proof. No raw IP stored (salted HMAC only).
#
# First visitor: freelancers and small agencies searching "free e-signature",
# "docusign alternative self hosted", "sign nda online free"; Indie Hackers, r/selfhosted,
# r/freelance. Volume not measured with an external tool.
#
# Path to revenue (payments stay off): free and MIT as the lead magnet; a hosted
# version, done-for-you setup (templates, PDF, reminders) or GitHub Sponsors are the
# paid steps -- hosting under the public name and billing are owner-gated.

hypotheses:
  - claim: >-
      Freelancers and small agencies will deploy their own signing-link server
      when the demo shows the certificate is verifiable, because per-envelope
      plans are the part of e-signature they resent for one-page agreements.
    status: untested
    checked: null
    evidence: customer-contact
  - claim: >-
      A document fingerprint plus a re-checkable /c/<token>.json is what makes a
      client accept a typed-name signature from a small shop, and the certificate
      (not the signing page) is what owners actually keep.
    status: untested
    checked: null
    evidence: customer-contact

economics:
  currency: USD
  mrr: null
  monthly_cost: 0
  customers: null

budget:
  monthly_cap: 1
  protected: false

kill_criteria:
  - Fewer than three distinct GitHub users (issues, stars, or a pasted report) engage within 90 days of the page being reachable from the published site.
  - A report that a signed document's text could be changed without the certificate flagging it, or that a signer's raw network address was stored; integrity and privacy come before any new feature.

links:
  production: https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/sign-keeper/
  analytics: null

fly.toml.text:
# Fly.io self-deploy, in your own account (needs flyctl and a card on file with Fly):
#   fly launch --copy-config --no-deploy --dockerfile Dockerfile
#   fly volumes create state --size 1
#   fly secrets set ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) IP_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
#   (optional settings from render.yaml, e.g. PUBLIC_URL, go in with `fly secrets set` too)
#   fly deploy
# One machine that never auto-stops: the state file lives on its volume.
app = "sign-keeper-CHANGE-ME"
primary_region = "iad"

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

[env]
  PORT = "8080"
  STATE = "/data/state.json"
  TRUST_PROXY = "true"

[mounts]
  source = "state"
  destination = "/data"

[http_service]
  internal_port = 8080
  force_https = true
  auto_stop_machines = "off"
  auto_start_machines = false
  min_machines_running = 1
  [[http_service.checks]]
    path = "/healthz"
    interval = "30s"
    timeout = "5s"

index.html.text:
Send a contract link. Get a signature you can prove wasn't changed.

Paste the text, send the link. The signer reads it, types their name and ticks a consent box. You get a certificate with the document's SHA-256 fingerprint and a hash-chained audit trail that anyone can re-check. It runs on your own server, with no per-envelope fee and no account for the signer.

Try the tamper check in your browser sample data

This runs entirely on this page with your browser's own crypto. Nothing is uploaded. The names and text are invented.

After signing, edit the text above and press Verify: the fingerprint will no longer match.

Not signed yet.

Why use this instead of what you do today

TodayCatchSign Keeper
DocuSign, PandaDoc, Dropbox SignPer-user or per-envelope plans; documents and audit trail live in their accountUnlimited requests, one JSON file you own, no fee
"Reply YES to confirm" by emailNo fingerprint of what was agreed, no recorded consent to e-signExact text hashed, consent wording stored, certificate to keep
Print, sign, scanSlow, easy to lose, no integrity checkLink, ninety seconds, verifiable record

Honest limits: typed-name (simple) signatures only; no identity verification, templates, field placement, PDF upload, reminders or multi-signer routing; one admin key. For regulated or high-value documents use a qualified provider.

Run it yourself

git clone https://github.com/Duncan-Haywood/oss-monorepo && cd oss-monorepo/ventures/sign-keeper
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) PUBLIC_URL=https://sign.example.com COMPANY_NAME=Acme node server.mjs

# create:   open https://sign.example.com/admin, paste the text, copy the signing link
# verify:   https://sign.example.com/c/<token>.json

One-click Render deploy and Docker are in the README.

Related tools

Pair with Testimonial Keeper to collect proof after the job and Dunning Engine to chase late invoices. Publishing a release? Changelog Keeper is the same self-hosted shape for release notes.

Questions

Is a typed-name signature legally valid?

In many places, including the US (ESIGN Act and UETA) and the EU/UK (eIDAS/ECA as a simple electronic signature), a typed name with clear intent to sign and a record of it is generally accepted for ordinary contracts. Some documents are excluded (wills, certain family-law and real-estate papers, notices a statute says must be on paper). Sign Keeper is not legal advice; check what your document needs.

Can someone alter a document after it is signed?

Not undetectably. The text has a SHA-256 fingerprint and every audit event hashes the one before it. The certificate page and /c/<token>.json recompute all of it from stored data and report any mismatch. It is tamper-evident, not tamper-proof: whoever controls your server can still delete the file, so keep certificate copies.

What does it store about the signer?

The typed name, the time, the consent wording they ticked and a salted HMAC of their network address that cannot be turned back into the address. Not a raw IP, not a device fingerprint.

How is this different from DocuSign or PandaDoc?

Those add identity checks, templates, bulk send, field placement and qualified signatures. Sign Keeper does one thing: send a link, collect a typed signature with consent, keep a verifiable certificate, on a server you own with no per-envelope fee.

No warranty. This tool and the server are provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied, and with no uptime or delivery guarantee. It is software, not legal advice, and it does not make any document enforceable. You are the operator: you decide whether an electronic signature is valid for your document and place.

render.yaml.text:
# One-click self-deploy: https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>
# Render builds the Dockerfile in YOUR account; nothing runs on the author's.
services:
  - type: web
    name: sign-keeper
    runtime: docker
    dockerContext: ventures/sign-keeper
    dockerfilePath: ventures/sign-keeper/Dockerfile
    plan: starter
    healthCheckPath: /healthz
    disk:
      name: state
      mountPath: /data
      sizeGB: 1
    envVars:
      - key: STATE
        value: /data/state.json
      - key: ADMIN_KEY
        generateValue: true
      - key: IP_SECRET
        generateValue: true
      - key: TRUST_PROXY
        value: "true"
      - key: PUBLIC_URL
        sync: false
      - key: COMPANY_NAME
        sync: false
      - key: BRAND_COLOR
        sync: false
      - key: NOTIFY_WEBHOOK
        sync: false
